why: The v0.7.0 release run was cancelled by its own 20-minute budget and the release shipped without provenance (D-196). Re-measured here because `ci.yml:test` **changed shape** rather than because the suite grew: its `Unit tests` step went from one process to four xdist workers with `--dist loadfile` (D-244, B-143). The serial observations recorded at the v0.12.0 boundary no longer describe the job that exists, so they are replaced rather than kept -- `update` below says which rule that is, and `docs/development.md` records why 'every recorded observation binds' is a rule about runs and not about a job that has been reshaped. The retired figures are kept in prose because the comparison is the point. The previous `why` made a narrow margin the headline: the worst serial leg was 3302s, 91.7% of the 3600s half-rule limit on the 120-minute ceiling, leaving 9.93 minutes of margin and a warning that the next wave must confront the ceiling rather than re-record past it. That framing is now this: the parallel job's worst leg is 2745s, which needs 91.50 minutes and leaves 28.50 minutes of margin against the same unchanged ceiling -- growth headroom of 31.1% where it was 9.0%. **The alarm is quieted, not removed, and the ceiling is deliberately not lowered to match the faster job**: a budget that follows every speed-up down loses the only thing it is for, which is reporting the next growth. The headroom is also far smaller than the change promised -- a twelve-core local measurement predicted the step at 0.2833 of serial and the four-vCPU runner measured 0.814 (B-143) -- so the next wave will meet this ceiling sooner than a local benchmark would suggest. No budget is raised or lowered by this re-record. Every ceiling still clears the half rule.
source: GitHub Actions REST API, read-only: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}. `seconds` is completed_at - started_at for the hosted job, including runner setup, checkout and post-steps -- the same wall clock bounded by job-level `timeout-minutes`.
half_rule: A budget must be at least twice the longest recorded duration of the job it bounds. Equivalently, when a measured gate exceeds half of an explicit timeout budget, raise or re-measure that budget before release.
update: Re-record before raising or lowering any budget and before every release wave that materially grows the suite. Use only completed jobs whose GitHub conclusion is exactly `success`; failed and cancelled runs stop early and therefore do not measure the work. Replace the affected job's observations with the newest representative successful sample, then run `python scripts/check_ci_budgets.py`.
conclusion: Every observation below records conclusion `success`. No failed, skipped or cancelled job is used for calibration.
not_claimed: This is a small operational sample, not a latency distribution or percentile estimate. The half-rule margin, rather than an inferred percentile, separates the observed maximum from the declared ceiling.

jobs.note: **Replaced, not appended.** The `Unit tests` step now runs `python -m pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile` (D-244, B-143), so the six serial legs recorded at the v0.12.0 boundary measure a job that no longer exists; keeping the slowest of them would bound a process count this job no longer uses. These are the newest successful run of the parallel job (33639322391), all three Python matrix legs of each because they share one job-level budget. **They are `workflow_dispatch` runs on the `feat/ci-suite-speed` branch, not post-merge `main` pushes** -- the four-worker job does not exist on `main` until that change lands, so no post-merge sample of it can exist yet, and the next release wave should re-record from `main` pushes. The worst leg is 2745s (45.75 min), against 3302s (55.03 min) for the serial job it replaces. This job, not release.yml:verify, is still the longest duration recorded anywhere in this file.
